chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan and Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Hashimi, from one of our companions, from Sulayman ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:

Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: 'The topknot on the head of the grouse is from the wiping of Sulayman ibn Dawud (peace be upon him). And that is, the male intended to copulate with its female, but she prevented him. So he said to her, "Do not prevent me, for I do not intend except that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, would extract from me a soul that would be remembered by you." So she answered him to what he sought.'

So when it wanted to lay eggs, he said to her, "Where do you want to lay eggs?" So she said to him, "I do not know, shall I move it away from the road?" He said to her, "I am afraid that the passers-by would pass by you, but I see for you that you should lay eggs near the road, so whoever sees you near it would think that you are picking seeds from the road." So she answered him to that and laid eggs, and incubated them until she oversaw the births.

So while the two of them were involved in that, when there noticed Sulayman ibn Dawud (peace be upon him) in his army, and the birds were shading him. So she said to him, "This is Sulayman who is coming over to us in his army, and there is no safety if he were to trample us, and trample our eggs." So he said to her, "Sulayman (peace be upon him) would be a merciful man with us, so is there anything with you to gift to him for (the safety of) your chicks when they are born?" She said, "Yes, a grasshopper which I hid from you, awaiting for my chicks for it when they are born. So is there anything with you?" He said, "Yes, I have a date with me, which I hid from you for my chicks."

She said, "So you take your date, and I take my grasshopper, and we go to Sulayman (peace be upon him) and we present these to him, for he is a man who loves the gifts." So he took the date in his beak, and she took the grasshopper in her claws, then they went to Sulayman (peace be upon him). So when he saw them both, and he was upon his throne, he extended his hands for them. So they went over and the male sat upon the right hand and the female sat upon the left hand, and he asked them both of their state. So they informed him.

So he accepted both their gifts, and diverted his army away from them and their eggs, and he wiped upon their heads, and supplicated for them both with the Blessings. So the topknot appeared on top of both their heads from the wiping of Sulayman (peace be upon him).

key_terms.الْقُنْزُعَةُ: The topknot or tuft of feathers on the head of the grouse
key_terms.سُلَيْمَانُ بْنُ دَاوُدَ: Sulayman ibn Dawud (Solomon son of David), a Prophet and King
key_terms.مَسْحَةٌ: Wiping (with the hand), a ritual or affectionate gesture

ai.seo_question: What is the origin of the topknot on the grouse's head according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the prophetic attribute of mercy (*rahmah*) in Sulayman ibn Dawud, linking his physical gesture of wiping the birds' heads to the biological feature of the grouse's topknot. In Shia tradition, this narrative serves as a *'alam* (sign) of divine providence, demonstrating how the righteous stewardship of creation is rewarded with lasting blessings and distinct physical marks.
